title: Policy Precedence Resolver
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Instrumentation
Configuration
Policy Precedence
LRS Runtime
description: A p5.js resolver in which learners set the book config, page option, metadata.json and ?xapi= URL switch layers, predict the resolved compact and teaching values, and watch the xAPI runtime's five-layer precedence resolve each key and name the layer that supplied it.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Policy precedence for the xAPI runtime's compact and teaching keys
learningObjectives: The learner will determine the final compact and teaching values for a MicroSim by applying the five policy layers in order, and will identify which layer supplied each value.
prerequisites: The LRS config file and teaching mode (Chapter 17)

accessibility.notes: All inputs are native selects, buttons and a checkbox; values are written as true, false or not set, not shown by color alone; color-blind-safe blue/vermillion for true/false

controls.label: Page option (layer 3)
controls.purpose: Set the policy option passed to LRSSim.create

controls.label: metadata.json (layer 4)
controls.purpose: Set the MicroSim's own xapi block

controls.label: URL switch (layer 5)
controls.purpose: Choose ?xapi= tokens: teaching, production, full, compact

controls.label: Resolve
controls.purpose: Animate the climb from layer 1 to layer 5

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return every layer to its starting state

controls.label: Show which layer won
controls.purpose: Label each resolved value with its source layer

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-resolve with an animated worked procedure and source attribution
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Layer configuration with step animation and labelled result
keyQuestions: Which layer is the highest one that sets this key?
Which file would you edit to change one MicroSim, the whole book, or one visit?
commonMisconceptions: A higher layer replaces the whole policy rather than resolving key by key
metadata.json always beats the URL switch
The book config is the highest-priority setting
assessmentOpportunities: Predicting resolved values and source layers before pressing Resolve
Designing a layer setup for a stated teaching goal

simulation.model: Per-key precedence resolution mirroring lrs-lite-sim.js loadPolicy() and urlPolicy()
equations: value(key) = first set value among URL switch, metadata.json, page option, book config, runtime defaults
assumptions: Timer keys (idleMs, offscreenMs, blurMs) are not shown
